translationRepairs: When Songgotu and Sonin once formed factions for private gain, the Kangxi Emperor removed them from key posts and set them aside—did he ever trust them again?
When Mingzhu and Songgotu once formed factions for private gain, the Kangxi Emperor removed them from key posts and set them aside—did he ever trust them again?
Chinese names 明珠 and 索額圖; idiomatic wrongly has Songgotu and Sonin (索尼).
In former days, when Songgotu and Sonin formed factions for private gain, the Sacred Ancestor removed them from key posts and placed them in idle positions—when did he ever trust them again?
In former days, when Mingzhu and Songgotu formed factions for private gain, the Sacred Ancestor removed them from key posts and placed them in idle positions—when did he ever trust them again?
Literal likewise mistranslates 明珠、索額圖 as Songgotu and Sonin.
If Long Keduo and Nian Gengyao do not learn fear and thoroughly reform, they must not imagine they can fare like Songgotu and Sonin!
If Long Keduo and Nian Gengyao do not learn fear and thoroughly reform, they must not imagine they can fare like Mingzhu and the others!
Chinese 明珠等; idiomatic wrongly repeats Songgotu and Sonin instead of Mingzhu and the others.

In year four, Long Keduo's servant Niulun was caught extorting bribes by abusing his master's power. Handed to the courts, the case revealed that Long Keduo had taken bribes from Gengyao, Governors Zhao Shixian and Manbao, and Governors-General Gan Guobi and Sukeji.

In year four, Long Keduo's servant Niulun was caught extorting bribes by abusing his master's power. Handed to the courts, the case revealed that Long Keduo had taken bribes from Gengyao, Governors-General Zhao Shixian and Manbao, and Governors Gan Guobi and Sukeji.
Chinese 總督趙世顯、滿保，巡撫甘國璧、蘇克濟 reverses the English office titles.

In the fourth year, Long Keduo's household servant Niulun, abusing his master's power, extorted bribes; when the matter came to light he was arrested and handed to the judicial authorities, and investigation revealed that Long Keduo had accepted bribes from Gengyao and from Governors Zhao Shixian and Manbao, and from Governors-General Gan Guobi and Sukeji.

In the fourth year, Long Keduo's household servant Niulun, abusing his master's power, extorted bribes; when the matter came to light he was arrested and handed to the judicial authorities, and investigation revealed that Long Keduo had accepted bribes from Gengyao and from Governors-General Zhao Shixian and Manbao, and from Governors Gan Guobi and Sukeji.
Literal repeats the same 總督/巡撫 office-title reversal.
That year, Tsewang Arabtan sent his general Tsewang Donduk to raid Tibet and kill the Dalai Lama's regent Lhabzang Khan.
That year, Tsewang Arabtan sent his general Tsewang Donduk to raid Tibet and kill Lhabzang Khan.
Chinese has only 拉藏汗; literal invents 'the Dalai Lama's regent'.

Praising Gengyao's keen administration, the emperor noted that a governor normally had no troop command; he was therefore specially appointed Governor of Sichuan with concurrent charge of governorship affairs.

Praising Gengyao's keen administration, the emperor noted that a provincial governor normally had no troop command; he was therefore specially appointed Governor-General of Sichuan while concurrently managing the governor's affairs.
Chinese 特授四川總督，兼管巡撫事: 總督 is governor-general, 巡撫 is governor; idiomatic collapses both to Governor.

The emperor praised Gengyao's keen and efficient administration; since a governor had no responsibility to command troops, he was specially appointed Governor of Sichuan while also retaining charge of governorship affairs.

The emperor praised Gengyao's keen and efficient administration; since a provincial governor had no responsibility to command troops, he was specially appointed Governor-General of Sichuan while also retaining charge of the governor's affairs.
Literal likewise mistranslates 總督 as Governor instead of Governor-General.
at Baoxian in southern Henan, transfer of a battalion commander from the Weimao garrison to hold the post;
at Baoxian south of the Great River (Dadu River), transfer of a battalion commander from the Weimao garrison to hold the post;
大河南保縣 refers to Baoxian south of the Dadu River on the Sichuan frontier, not Henan province.
Gengyao memorialized on frontier defense, asking for an earthen fort at the Zhongdu River crossing beyond Dartsedo and transfer of the Lanzhou garrison commander to hold it;
Gengyao memorialized on frontier defense, asking for an earthen fort at the Zhongdu River crossing beyond Dartsedo and transfer of the Lan Prefecture (嵐州) garrison commander to hold it;
嵐州 is Lan Prefecture, not 蘭州 Lanzhou; the idiomatic English conflates the place names.

In year sixty-one Gengyao secretly reported that the Tibetan lama Chuerqimu Zangbu and Prefect Shi Rujin portrayed Tsewang Norbu as slack, while Vice Commander Chang Ling, Reader-in-Waiting Mandu, Department Director Batma, and others acted arbitrarily, sowing discord among the garrison in Tibet."

In year sixty-one Gengyao secretly reported that the Tibetan lama Chuerqimu Zangbu and Prefect Shi Rujin portrayed Tsewang Norbu as slack, while Vice Commander Chang Ling, Reader-in-Waiting Mandu, Department Director Batma, and others acted arbitrarily, sowing discord among the garrison in Tibet.
Idiomatic English has a stray closing quote with no matching opener.
Qinghai taiji Sonam Dash, lured and captured by Lobzang Danjin, escaped and submitted; Gengyao reported it; the court enfeoffed him as beile and ordered Gengyao to reassure him.
Qinghai taiji Sonam Dash, lured and captured by Lobzang Danjin, escaped and submitted; Gengyao reported it; the court enfeoffed him as beise and ordered Gengyao to reassure him.
貝子 corresponds to beise, not beile (貝勒); the idiomatic English misrenders the noble rank.

Gengyao ordered Zhongqi to lead Was and Zagun native troops to Guide Fort, pacify Sidongcebu, annihilate the Chenku division, capture and execute the Wo'erjia chieftain, and accept the rest in surrender.

Gengyao ordered Zhongqi to lead Was and Zagun native troops to Guide Fort, pacify upper and lower monastery Sidongcebu, annihilate the Chenku division, capture and execute the Wo'erjia chieftain, and accept the rest in surrender.
Idiomatic omits 上下寺 from 撫定上下寺東策布; the literal retains upper and lower monastery Sidongcebu.
In year two, finding Lobzang Danjin's rebellion unpardonable, the court appointed Zhongqi Valiant General and urged Gengyao to advance.
In year two, finding Lobzang Danjin's rebellion unpardonable, the emperor appointed Zhongqi Valiant General and urged Gengyao to advance.
Chinese 上 denotes the emperor; idiomatic wrongly substitutes collective "the court".
Gengyao's retainers Zou Lu and Wang Jingqi were executed in turn; his relatives were distributed as bond-servants in the banners.
Gengyao's retainers Zou Lu and Wang Jingqi were executed in turn; their relatives were distributed as bond-servants in the banners.
Chinese 親屬 follows 鄒魯、汪景祺坐斬 and denotes the retainers' kin under collective punishment, not Gengyao's; English 'his' wrongly points to Gengyao.
His father Xianzheng entered service through hereditary privilege as a Censorate clerk and rose to Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner.
His father Xianzheng entered service through hereditary privilege as a Censorate clerk and rose to Hubei Provincial Administration Commissioner.
Source has 湖北布政使 (Hubei), not Huguang; idiomatic incorrectly expands to Huguang.
His father Xianzheng, starting from a yinsheng appointment as clerk of the Censorate, rose to Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner.
His father Xianzheng, starting from a yinsheng appointment as clerk of the Censorate, rose to Hubei Provincial Administration Commissioner.
Source has 湖北布政使 (Hubei); literal incorrectly says Huguang.
Zhongqi was appointed acting governor-general and ordered to take charge of the Pacification General-in-Chief's seal.
Yue Zhongqi was appointed acting governor-general and ordered to take charge of the Pacification General-in-Chief's seal.
Chinese 鍾琪 is the given name of 岳鍾琪; literal omits the surname already established in the chapter.
